collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Someone smashed a villager's canoe in a quarrel: ask for restitution, or let the village decide.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: In a furious quarrel, (friend) smashed the bow of (subject)'s canoe. The village is angry and some want (friend) punished harshly. (subject), the one who was wronged, has asked to be heard first. (subject.He/she) does not want revenge. What should (subject) ask for?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) asks for (friend) to rebuild the canoe, with (subject) beside (friend.him/her), every day until it is done. (friend) agrees, red-faced. It takes a month. They talk a lot. By the end, they have agreed on rules for the next quarrel: walk away first.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) says (subject.he/she) will accept what the village decides. The village asks (friend) to replace the canoe and give up the next festival. (friend) accepts. (subject) wishes (subject.he/she) had asked for something that brought them together instead.
